title: Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut, Deir el-Bahari
summary: The Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut (Djeser-Djeseru) at Deir el-Bahari is a monumental rock-cut terraced sanctuary constructed during the Eighteenth Dynasty for the female pharaoh Hatshepsut and her father Thutmose I. Set beneath dramatic limestone cliffs on the west bank of the Nile opposite Karnak, its three rising colonnaded terraces and painted reliefs celebrating her divine birth and expedition to Punt represent a pinnacle of ancient Egyptian New Kingdom classical architecture.

uncertainty.note: Constructed during Hatshepsut's reign; Egypt Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities dates the temple to c. 1473-1458 BC (astronomical -1472 to -1457). Standing today.
